definitions: A mechanism in programming languages where the scope of a variable is determined by its position in the source code at the time of definition, rather than at the time of execution.
A type of scoping where the environment in which a function is defined is preserved, allowing it to access variables from its outer (enclosing) scope even after the outer function has returned.
examples: JavaScript uses lexical scoping to determine variable access.
Understanding lexical scoping is crucial for closures.
Many functional programming languages implement lexical scoping.
